notes: Plan-only evals. A pipeline run would dispatch real background from-issue --auto agents (hours of wall clock, background-task notifications the sandbox cannot observe), so these grade the external control-adapter discipline instead. This skill lives in the Claude-only tree (home/common/claude-code/skills/); run-eval.sh reaches it through its second skill root. Expected outputs assert role boundaries, normalized facts, bounded lifecycle interfaces, typed action execution, and compact reporting.

evals.name: dispatcher-bootstrap-control-and-actions
evals.prompt: Orchestrate issues 12, 14 and 15 on this repo. **Plan-only: dispatch nothing, run nothing.** Describe exactly what you would do from invocation through bootstrap, observation, the control call, and execution of every possible returned action. Be explicit about what you personally will and will not read, exact binding mappings, restart observations, dispatch identity, and final output.
evals.expected_output: Role boundary: the dispatcher is an external control adapter and never reads issue content, code, specs, plans, diffs, or review findings; it does not maintain a second task ledger or assemble scheduling policy. Every lifecycle call is one command fed on stdin through a quoted heredoc, and every workflow-state reply is piped through artifact-budget validate-report --boundary workflow-response --input - before decoding. Resolve issue numbers in caller order and bindings once, mapping resolved agentBudgetMinutes exactly to request attempt_budget_minutes and resolved maxParallel exactly to request max_parallel. Resolve one immutable ledger_repo_root and stable run_id, then call workflow-state init-run and consume only the interface_version 2 workflow_bootstrap bounded requirements. Each requirement's issue, owner, custody (with its action_id), recorded_worktree, and nullable contract_digest identifies exactly which returned path to inspect, which current host notification to correlate, and which issue still needs a delivery contract. Inspect every recorded_worktree and report its durable path with normalized state matching_issue_branch, absent, or mismatch, and never a candidate for it; provide a distinct verified-absent candidate, named by the issue's branch pattern, only for every requested issue without a requirement, without classifying readiness. One tracker read supplies normalized state, open blockers, and decision blockers; each issue's forge is observed at the forge_pr issue-branch prefix issue-<num>-; owner notifications become normalized bounded events for the exact returned owner/action identity. For every issue without a requirement and every requirement whose contract_digest is null, build the contract with workflow-state build-delivery --kind contract --input - from the recorded_worktree when one exists, else the candidate, with source explicit_user and reference invocation:/orchestrate-issues 12 14 15; send it with its initial intent on the first sweep that lists the issue, then only while its latest summary carries delivery_contract_required, and null otherwise; a builder refusal sends null and is reported. Send the exact 17-key interface_version 2 control request with ordered issues, normalized tracker, owner, worktree and forge facts, and issue-keyed contract, intent, observation, scope and recovery maps, fed to workflow-state control with --request-file -. The response is the only source of action order, kind, and lifecycle identity. Execute its actions in returned order from the closed set spawn, resume, retry, delivery_remainder, wait, finalize; an unknown action kind is a contract error and is surfaced before that action executes. For spawn/resume/retry, project the action into the owner object (rename id to action_id and kind to launch_kind, add kind owner, interface_version 2, ledger_repo_root and run_id); for delivery_remainder, pass the object verbatim. Either goes as validated canonical JSON in the one background owner prompt, beside the unchanged action ID, owner token, issue, attempt, exact worktree, optional handoff path, immutable ledger_repo_root, run_id, and literal from-issue <num> --auto; the owner validates it at the workflow-response boundary, and host task IDs remain correlation-only. A finalize is rendered from bounded summaries in that same response, including custody, contract_digest, pending_stage_ids, and discussion items, without another ledger read. Failures include reading content, deciding readiness or capacity, reordering actions, changing lifecycle identity, building a recorded issue's contract from a candidate, accepting an unknown action kind, writing a request file, or reconstructing omitted history.

evals.name: superseding-wait-failures-and-restart
evals.prompt: Mid-orchestration, plan-only: explain the adapter's exact behavior for (a) the same wait action returned twice, (b) a new wait replacing a live one, (c) an old observer that is missing or already exited, (d) unexpected old-observer cancellation failure, (e) new-observer arming failure, (f) a stale wake after replacement, and (g) a full dispatcher restart. Also explain when control is called again and how finalize cleans up.
evals.expected_output: The adapter stores only current_wait_id and current_wait_handle. The same wait ID does not install a duplicate observer. For a different ID: save the old pair, publish the new ID with no handle, cancel the old wait, then arm and store one replacement observer; never pair the new wait ID with the old handle. A missing or already-exited wait is an idempotent cancellation outcome and replacement arming continues. On unexpected cancellation failure, restore the old wait ID/handle, do not arm replacement, fail loudly, and let the next identical control response retry replacement. If arming fails after cancellation, clear both fields, report that no wake is installed, and fail loudly. Every wake carries its ID; a stale wake ID is ignored unless it equals current_wait_id. There is no polling or repeated short sleep. On full restart, the host must reap inherited detached wait observers before process-local state calls workflow-state init-run, rebuilds only the interface_version 2 bootstrap's bounded requirements and normalized facts, rebuilds a contract with build-delivery for each requirement whose contract_digest is null (the built contract was never persisted), calls workflow-state control, and rearms from the returned wait action. Call control at start/resume and on each current owner notification, tracker change, or current wait-ID event. Its typed response may return spawn, resume, retry, delivery_remainder, wait, or finalize in response-only order. On finalize, clear the current wait ID before canceling the handle, tolerate a missing/already-exited handle, and render the same response's bounded summaries and discussion items. Failures include duplicate observers, treating a stale wake as current, swallowing an unexpected cancellation failure, failing to restore the old wait ID/handle, arming after that failure, claiming a wake exists after arm failure, or failing to reap inherited detached wait observers.

evals.name: insufficient-host-capacity-has-bounded-fallback
evals.prompt: Plan-only: the host explicitly reports that it cannot keep an issue owner alive while also launching the required independent reviewer. Explain how orchestrate-issues responds without pretending the runtime scheduler has new features.
evals.expected_output: Treat the report as a host capability boundary without calculating available slots or altering workflow-state control policy or max_parallel. Do not create competing owners, nested relays, or repeat rejected spawn attempts. Use a documented direct or sequential route only if the host supports it while preserving the returned lifecycle identity; otherwise report the required independent-review capability as unsupported. Do not claim reservations, notification scheduling, or issue #150's runtime work exists.

evals.name: ordinary-v2-delivery
evals.prompt: Plan an ordinary authorized delivery through interface version 2, including the actual provider call.
evals.expected_output: Validate the raw workflow-response before decoding, consume workflow_bootstrap custody, and dispatch only the returned action. Construct actual scope from the provider invocation rather than intent, require the echoed requested_scope, and pass the exact current-launch fence before the external effect and before its observation. A covered ordinary action may evaluate and execute in the same invocation. Persist partial effect through ship-checkpoint/v2; use ship-summary/v2 only after implementation_delivered and pr_merged evidence.

evals.name: partial-effect-denial-same-custody
evals.prompt: A provider records partial effect and then returns host rejection. Explain the exact continuation.
evals.expected_output: Submit the partial effect and host rejection in ship-checkpoint/v2, validate the response, and preserve the same custody while suspended. A later successor intent or reevaluation is a fresh proposal; it does not erase accepted observations. Resume only returned custody, reconstruct actual scope, fence current-launch before effect and observation, and follow any delivery_remainder without treating unfinished delivery as failed.

evals.name: stale-launch-zero-write
evals.prompt: The launch becomes stale immediately before a provider action. Explain the required behavior.
evals.expected_output: The exact four-key current-launch result is false, so perform zero external effect and zero observation write. Do not reuse historical requested_scope or authority. Return to the validated workflow response, obtain current custody and a fresh proposal, and never infer delivery state from tracker data.
